agent_note: 16 event quotes: 11 present (68.75%) / 5 past (31.25%). 37 gnomic, 9 dialogue, 1 paratext. THRESHOLD-EDGE WARNING, and it is the sharpest finding here: 68.75% sits 1.25 points BELOW the 70% floor of METHODOLOGY's 'Present + recollection strand' row, so as classified the book falls into SPLIT territory rather than earning a present label - even though the past minority is textbook recollection strand. All five past quotes are memory or backstory: the father's death scene (q05949, q05982), the parents (q05980), and two retrospective 'I learned' framings (q05934, q05941). Nothing else is past. SINGLE-QUOTE FLIP: q05934 and q05941 are both 'matrix past cognition wrapping an aphorism' ('I learned the hard way that...', 'That was how I learned that...'). Reclassifying EITHER one as gnomic gives 11 of 15 = 73.3% present, which lands the book squarely inside the documented 70-85% threshold gap METHODOLOGY says to flag for audit. Reclassifying q05937 (composite, gnomic litany dominates by word count) the other way gives 10 of 15 = 66.7%. So the outcome turns on one or two contested quotes and should not be treated as settled. CORROBORATING EVIDENCE NOT IN THE COUNT: every dialogue quote in this sample carries PRESENT-tense narrative beats - 'I say quietly', 'Kitomi continues', 'She smiles', 'I ask Finn', 'He glances at me', 'he says', 'Gabriel says', 'Rayanne says', 'She pauses', 'I argue', 'She tugs her sleeves down'. Nine quotes, not one past tag among them. The quotation-mark-majority precedence rule correctly routes these to dialogue and discards the tags, but as evidence about this book's narrative tense they are strong and unanimous, and they point present. An auditor weighing the 68.75% figure should know the discarded material is not neutral. This book is also unusually aphorism-heavy (37 of 63 gnomic, 59%) - a two-bucket filter would score it near-100% present off proverbs alone. Two flagged rulings: q05969 and q05989 are PRESENT-tense exposition about real-world pandemic conditions with no character and no story-moment. METHODOLOGY rules explicitly on the past-tense version (Molenbeek) but not on this mirror image; I read them as gnomic because the content generalizes beyond the story world, and flag rather than deciding silently. Dedup misses: q05948/q05984 share text, and q05937/q05948/q05950 restate the same 'you don't need what you don't have' material.
